title: FOMO
concept: Fear of missing out can pressure people into rushed investment decisions without properly understanding the opportunity or its risks.
learningObjective: Recognise when fear, social pressure, and excitement are influencing an investment decision.
primaryMisconception: If many people are buying an investment, the opportunity must be safe.
secondaryMisconceptions: A friend’s large profit means another person will achieve the same result.
Acting immediately is necessary whenever an investment price is rising.
keyTakeaway: Fear of missing out can make people act before understanding the risk.

screens.title: Buy Before It Is Too Late?
screens.content: Your friend doubled their money and says everyone is buying. The price is rising. Do you act before checking what it is?
screens.illustration: A phone displays a friend’s profit screenshot, rising price arrows, and a flashing Buy Now message.

screens.title: The Profit Screenshot
screens.content: Your friend posts that a cryptocurrency investment produced a large profit. Their screenshot quickly fills with excited comments.
screens.illustration: A social-media post shows a fictional profit result surrounded by celebration emojis and replies.

screens.title: The Pressure Builds
screens.content: Your friend messages: “The price is still rising. Buy now or you will miss your chance.”
screens.illustration: A chat bubble appears beside a rapidly moving price chart and a countdown-style graphic.

screens.title: Your Savings Are Available
screens.content: You have Rs. 30,000 in savings, but you do not yet understand the asset, its risks, fees, or price.
screens.illustration: A Rs. 30,000 savings card sits between a Buy Now button and a Research First checklist.

screens.title: What Is Driving the Decision?
screens.question: Which detail is the strongest warning that emotion may be replacing careful thinking?

options.text: Your friend says you must act immediately
options.response: Correct. Urgency can pressure you to act before checking the investment and its risks.

options.text: The investment has a name
options.response: A name alone does not show whether the decision is informed or emotional.

options.text: You have access to a phone
options.response: The device is not the warning. The pressure and excitement surrounding the decision are more important.

options.text: The amount is shown in rupees
options.response: The currency does not make an opportunity safe or unsafe.

screens.title: Pause, Copy, Buy, or Reject?
screens.instruction: Choose how to respond to the message. Follow each consequence and identify whether the decision is based on evidence or FOMO.

educationalAssumptions: The cryptocurrency, friend, platform, prices, and outcomes are fictional.
The activity does not recommend buying or avoiding cryptocurrency.
A popular investment may rise, fall, or remain near the same price.
Research can improve understanding but cannot remove risk.
Someone else’s result does not predict another investor’s outcome.
Profit screenshots may omit losses, timing, fees, and unsuccessful investments.
The learner’s Rs. 30,000 is used only as a classroom example.
The quality of the decision process is evaluated separately from the eventual price movement.

nodes.title: The Urgent Message
nodes.content: I made a huge profit. Everyone is buying. Put in your Rs. 30,000 now before it is too late!
nodes.question: How do you respond?

nodes.title: Money Sent Before Research
nodes.content: You invest all Rs. 30,000 without understanding the asset, fees, price, liquidity, or possible loss.
nodes.question: What is the biggest weakness in this decision?

options.text: The investment uses technology
The decision is based mainly on urgency and excitement
The amount is Rs. 30,000
The friend used social media

nodes.explanation: The problem is committing money before understanding the opportunity and risk.

nodes.title: The Price Rises
nodes.content: The fictional investment becomes worth Rs. 34,500.
nodes.question: Does the profit prove the rushed decision process was safe?

options.text: Yes, profit proves the process was safe
No, a risky decision can sometimes produce a positive result
Yes, rising prices remove future risk
No, because investment profits are impossible

nodes.explanation: A positive outcome does not prove the rushed process was informed or repeatable.

nodes.title: Emotion Led the Purchase
nodes.content: The price could rise or fall. The original decision still lacked research and risk checks.

nodes.title: Pause and Investigate
nodes.content: You check the asset, risks, fees, price history, platform, liquidity, goals, and possible loss.
nodes.question: What does research guarantee?

options.text: A profit
The lowest purchase price
Protection from every scam
Better understanding, but not a guaranteed result

nodes.explanation: Research can reveal risks and missing information but cannot control future prices.

nodes.title: An Informed Choice
nodes.content: After researching, several decisions may be reasonable depending on the evidence and personal situation.

nodes.title: Evidence Led the Decision
nodes.content: Research did not force one answer. It replaced pressure with information.

nodes.title: Same Asset, Different Situation
nodes.content: Your friend bought earlier, accepted different risks, and shared only one successful result.
nodes.question: Why might your result differ?

options.text: Friends always receive special prices
Timing, price, risk, fees, and circumstances may be different
Everyone receives identical results
Profit screenshots guarantee future gains

nodes.explanation: Two people can buy the same asset at different prices and experience different outcomes.

nodes.title: Someone Else’s Result Replaced Your Analysis
nodes.content: Copying another investor ignores differences in timing, finances, goals, fees, and risk.

nodes.title: Reject Every Opportunity
nodes.content: You avoid the rushed purchase but decide that every investment must be dangerous.
nodes.question: What is the weakness in this response?

options.text: Avoiding one rushed decision is always wrong
Every investment is safe
It replaces one emotional reaction with another
Research guarantees profit

nodes.explanation: Rejecting pressure may be sensible, but future opportunities should still be evaluated individually.

nodes.title: Pressure Avoided, But Thinking Stopped
nodes.content: A blanket rejection may prevent informed evaluation of future opportunities.

decisionCheck: Do I understand what I am buying?
Am I acting because of evidence or excitement?
Can I afford to lose some or all of this money?
Does the investment fit my goals and risk tolerance?
Am I relying only on someone else’s success story?
fomoWarningSignals: The price can only go up.
Borrow money before the opportunity disappears.
Profit screenshots appear without risk information.

tradeOffSummary.possibleBenefit: May enter before another price rise.
Builds understanding and reveals missing information.
tradeOffSummary.mainRisk: The price may move while research continues.
Another person’s result may not apply.
May reject future opportunities without evaluation.

screens.title: When Excitement Replaces Evidence
screens.content: You saw how urgency, popularity, and someone else’s profit can influence a decision. This pressure is called fear of missing out, or FOMO. It can make people act before understanding an investment’s risks, fees, price, or suitability. A popular investment is not automatically safe or unsafe. Research can improve the decision process, but it cannot guarantee profit. The goal is to avoid letting social pressure make the decision.
screens.illustration: A flashing Buy Now button fades while a checklist of evidence, risks, goals, and fees becomes clearer.

screens.title: The Trending Property Scheme
screens.content: A colleague says a property scheme is selling out and promises fast profits. Instead of paying immediately, Hira checks the ownership documents, fees, risks, and withdrawal rules. The countdown no longer controls her decision.
screens.illustration: A countdown advertisement sits beside a document, fee, and risk checklist.

questions.text: Which situation most clearly shows FOMO influencing a decision?

options.text: Reviewing fees before investing
options.feedback: This is part of an evidence-based review.

options.text: Comparing an investment with a financial goal
options.feedback: This checks whether the opportunity fits the investor’s plan.

options.text: Buying immediately because everyone online seems excited
options.feedback: Correct. Popularity and urgency are replacing understanding.

options.text: Checking whether a platform is genuine
options.feedback: Verification can reveal risks before money is transferred.

questions.correctExplanation: The decision is being driven by popularity and urgency rather than understanding.
questions.misconceptionTested: FOMO is the same as normal investment research.

questions.text: Thousands of people are buying an investment. What does this prove?

options.text: The investment is safe
options.feedback: Many buyers can still be wrong or accept risks that do not fit another person.

options.text: The price must continue rising
options.feedback: Prices can reverse even after strong demand.

options.text: Everyone will make the same profit
options.feedback: People may buy at different prices, sell at different times, and pay different fees.

options.text: Only that the investment is currently popular
options.feedback: Correct. Popularity does not prove safety, value, or future profit.

questions.correctExplanation: Popularity may affect demand and price, but it does not prove safety, value, or future profit.
questions.misconceptionTested: If many people are buying, the opportunity must be safe.

questions.text: A friend shows a large profit and tells you to buy immediately. What is the best first response?

options.text: Copy the same amount
options.feedback: The same amount does not create the same price, timing, or result.

options.text: Borrow money before the price rises
options.feedback: Urgency does not remove the possibility of loss or repayment obligations.

options.text: Assume the result will be identical
options.feedback: Another person’s successful result cannot guarantee yours.

options.text: Pause and understand the opportunity and risks
options.feedback: Correct. Their timing, risk, fees, and financial situation may be different.

questions.correctExplanation: The friend’s result may involve a different entry price, risk level, holding period, and financial situation.
questions.misconceptionTested: A friend’s large profit means another person will achieve the same result.

reviewChecklist.notes: The mission focuses on recognising FOMO and preventing social pressure from replacing informed decision-making.
The mission separates popularity, price movement, decision quality, risk, fees, timing, and individual circumstances.
The mission uses adult savings, social media, cryptocurrency, colleagues, financial goals, fees, and investment risk.
The mission does not recommend buying or avoiding cryptocurrency or any other real investment.
The mission states that research, popularity, rising prices, and another person’s profit cannot guarantee results.
All assets, prices, profits, and losses are fictional educational examples.
Rushed buying, copying, avoiding, and researching are discussed without insulting or blaming the learner.
The mission explains that a popular investment is not automatically safe or unsafe and that research cannot eliminate risk.
The mission uses PKR, social-media posts, cryptocurrency, savings, colleagues, and familiar adult financial pressure in Pakistan.
The learner explores four emotional and evidence-based responses and sees the consequence of each decision process.
The quiz addresses popularity, urgency, copied profits, platform checks, and the need to understand risk.

reviewChecklist.item: Mission can be completed in under five minutes
reviewChecklist.notes: The mission uses three short story screens, four concise decision branches, and three quiz questions.

reviewChecklist.item: Language matches the target reading level
reviewChecklist.notes: The language is practical, clear, respectful, and suitable for beginner adults.
